cards.explanation: The answer is everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ. The writer says, “Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God…” (1 John 5:1). Look at what's missing from that sentence, friends. No secret handshake, no membership card, no punch card with ten stamps. It's belief in Jesus, and that's the door.

The answer is when we love God and keep His commandments. The writer says, “By this we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and keep His commandments.” (1 John 5:2). Think about it this way, friends. If I told you I love my ovens and then never turned one on, you'd squint at me. The love and the keeping go together.

The answer is False. The writer says, “And His commandments are not burdensome…” (1 John 5:3). Not burdensome means they aren't a heavy load to haul around, friends. He's saying they don't weigh you down.

The answer is that everyone born of God overcomes the world. Watch the little word that opens verse 4, friends, “because.” The writer says the commandments aren't burdensome “…because everyone born of God overcomes the world.” (1 John 5:4). I think the point is that a load feels different depending on who's carrying it, and someone born of God has already overcome the world, so what God asks doesn't crush them.

The answer is faith. The writer says, “And this is the victory that has overcome the world: our faith.” (1 John 5:4). Notice what the victory is, friends. It's not a muscle or a trophy or a fancy title. It's our faith.

The answer is True. The writer asks who overcomes the world, then answers: “Only he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God.” (1 John 5:5). Notice the question comes right after he calls our faith the victory in verse 4, friends. So the one who overcomes is the one who believes.
The answer is blood. The writer says Jesus Christ came “…not by water alone, but by water and blood.” (1 John 5:6). He's careful to say both, friends. Water and blood, side by side.

The answer is the Spirit. The writer says, “And it is the Spirit who testifies to this, because the Spirit is the truth.” (1 John 5:6). He even says why the Spirit's word can be trusted, friends. The Spirit is the truth.

The answer is True. The writer says the Spirit, the water and the blood are three that testify, “…and these three are in agreement.” (1 John 5:8). You know how you ask three friends for directions and get three different routes? Not here, bakers. The three line up.

The answer is that it is greater. The writer says, “Even if we accept human testimony, the testimony of God is greater.” (1 John 5:9). People's word can count for something, friends, and God's testimony is greater still. He goes on to say what that testimony is.

The answer is liar. The writer says whoever “…does not believe God has made Him out to be a liar…” (1 John 5:10). That's a strong word, friends, and he means it plainly. He ties it to not believing the testimony God has given about His Son.

The answer is eternal life. The writer says, “And this is that testimony: God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.” (1 John 5:11). Eternal life is what God has given us, bakers. Hang onto that one.

The answer is Son. The writer says, “God has given us eternal life, and this life is in His Son.” (1 John 5:11). Then verse 12 goes on to say, “Whoever has the Son has life…” The life is found in the Son, friends.

The answer is False. The writer says, “Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.” (1 John 5:12). It's a heavy line, friends, and I think it's meant to be read slowly. No loopholes in either half of that verse.
